pr.title: Spec requests in the inbox for work only the person can do
pr.head: 86a52325d2d0ca5af94aa50814fbb111f08d5ac1

summary: Projector's inbox is where an agent puts things the person must not miss. It is a store of items for each session, which the project inbox CLI writes and Projector's panel lists above the Claude Code prompt. Today an item is either a question, whose answer goes back to the agent as a line such as ANSWER 3.a, or a notice, which sends nothing back.

Neither kind fits work that only the person can do, such as testing a build on their phone. Issue #366 describes a session where one such hand-off took a question, an install, a notice, and a typed reply. This pull request adds the plan for a third kind of item, a request, as the nested project inbox/requests under the completed inbox plan. The plan is at ready and now, and this pull request changes no code.

1. Layer 1: done and decline. An agent posts a request with steps. The person does the work and presses done or decline, which put the quoted request in the prompt with Done or Declined under it, so the person's notes travel with the outcome.
  2. Layer 2: start. A request can also carry a start action, such as installing a build. Pressing start sends the agent STARTED, quoting that action, as the person's consent to it. The agent then marks the request ready, or blocked with a reason the person reads before pressing retry.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Claim: a short-lived token a deliverer takes on an item before it sends the item's line, so that two deliverers never send the same line.
  • restoredAt: today's one field that lets an open item owe its agent a line, RESTORED. The plan's started field works the same way.
  • Ask rule: a permission rule that project init writes, which makes Claude Code ask the person before an agent runs a command that records the person's choice.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first review, of 86a5232, opened two threads:

  • § 2.3 changes a project inbox context command that doesn't exist.
  • start records the start action as the store holds it, so a press on a drawer that hasn't caught up with a revision consents to an action the person never saw.

It also lists five suggestions, and the repository's full gate passes at this head.

groups.title: The request plan
groups.kicker: A third inbox item that carries a hand-off from post to result
intro: The plan adds a request to the inbox's existing store rather than building a new mechanism. A request is numbered with questions and notices, listed in the same panel, snoozed and restored the same way, and delivered by the same claim-and-settle steps.

Read § 2.1 for the flow, § 2.2 for the stored fields, and § 2.3 for the CLI. § 3 gives the reasons, and its consent rule matters most: pressing start consents to the start action as it read at that moment and to nothing else, and start, done, and decline become ask rules, so that an agent can't record the person's consent itself.

checks.text: project show inbox/requests --json loads the plan as ready and now, and project check passes at this head and with main's CLI. The completed parent plan is untouched.

files.note: The whole plan: the problem, the flow and its two layers, the store fields, the CLI and Claude Code tools, the files to change, and the acceptance criteria.

checks.text: start runs project inbox start <number>, which records the start action as the store holds it. An agent's revise --start through the shell reaches the panel only at its next store read, up to 5 seconds later. A press in that window sends STARTED with an action the person never saw, which breaks § 3's consent rule. The review asks start to take the action the drawer shows and to refuse a mismatch.
A request owes its agent a line in three cases: an undelivered outcome, an undelivered RESTORED, and an undelivered STARTED. The existing claim and settle commands handle all three.

project inbox has no context subcommand at the base or on main. The note that names a subagent is the prompt hook's context, written by relayNote in hooks/inbox.ts. The review asks to drop context from this row and from § 2.5.

answer, dismiss, and snooze are the ask rules in src/projector/permissions.py today. Adding start, done, and decline there follows the same pattern, and the panel runs them outside an agent's shell, so the person is never asked.

is_restorable and restore in src/projector/inbox.py accept any dismissal that wasn't withdrawn. Storing a decline as dismissed with declined lets a declined request be restored, with RESTORED sent when the agent already heard DECLINED.
